**<mark>ICSG PRESS RELEASE Date Issued: 23</mark>**<sup>**rd**</sup> **<mark>November 2009</mark>** 



# **Copper: Preliminary Data for August 2009** 

The International Copper Study Group (ICSG) released preliminary data for August world copper supply and demand in its November 2009 Copper Bulletin.  The Bulletin is available for sale upon request. 

A decline in Chinese apparent usage<sup>*****</sup> based on lower net imports of refined copper and a decrease in EU apparent usage over the traditional holiday period led to an apparent refined copper market surplus in August of around 150,000 metric tonnes (t).  When making seasonal adjustments for world refined production and usage, August showed a surplus of about 90,000 t. The apparent refined copper balance for the first 8 months of 2009, including revisions to data previously presented, indicates a production deficit of 32,000 t (a seasonally adjusted surplus of 160,000 t). This compares with a production deficit of 117,000 t (a seasonally adjusted surplus of 72,000 t) for the same period in 2008. 

In the first 8 months of 2009, world usage is estimated to have decreased by 1.5% compared with that in the same period of 2008.  A strong increase in Chinese apparent usage (+45%) was insufficient to offset a decrease of 19% [1.7 million tons (Mt)] in the rest of the world.  Chinese apparent usage increased by 1.5 Mt in the first 8 months of 2009, compared with usage in the same period of 2008.<sup>*****</sup> Copper usage in the other important markets, the EU-15 countries, Japan, and the United States, decreased by 23%, 34%, and 23%, respectively. These three regions currently represent about 29% of total world copper usage. 

World mine production grew by 3% in the first 8 months of 2009 compared with that in the same period of 2008: Concentrate production grew by 1.9% while solvent extraction-electrowinning (SX-EW) was up by 7.2%. Indonesia, where production increased by 304,000 t (recovering from 2008 operational constraints), was the main contributor to production growth. Lower output in the two leading world producers, Chile and the United States, as well as Canada, which totalled about 180,000 t, partially offset growth in other countries.  The capacity utilization rate in August was 79.7%, slightly above the average of the previous 7 months. 

In the first 8 months of 2009, world refined production decreased by 0.8% compared with that in the same period of 2008: Primary production decreased by 0.5% while secondary production (from scrap) decreased by 3%, reflecting the global scarcity of scrap in the early part of the year.  Announced production cuts led to decreases in refined production of around 6% in Europe, 12% in North America, and 1% in Asia (ex-China). Increases of around 9% in Chile and 4% in China were not sufficient to offset decreases in the other regions. Refined production capacity utilization fell to 77.2% compared with an average rate of 81% in the same period of 2008.

The average LME cash price for October 2009 was US$6,287.98 per tonne, up from the September 2009 average of US$6,196.43 per tonne. The 2009 high and low copper prices through the end of September were US$6,675.5 and US$3,050.50 per tonne, respectively, and the average was US$4,832.16 per tonne. As of the end October 2009, copper stocks held at the major metal exchanges (LME, COMEX, SHFE) totalled 531,209 t, an increase of 141,526 t from stocks held at the end of December 2008. Compared to the September levels, stocks were up at all three exchanges (SHFE, LME, and COMEX).
